SOURCE: "Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions", Harsh Trivedi, Niranjan Balasubramanian, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal. ACL 2023 (Long Papers, pp. 10014–10037); arXiv 2212.10509. Code: github.com/stonybrooknlp/ircot
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/sources/trivedi-2023-interleaving-retrieval-chain-thought-reasoning.pdf

COVERAGE: Read chars 0–66,000 of 86,569 word for word. That covers the main paper, Limitations, Ethics, all references, and Appendices A–F with Tables 3–6. I skimmed chars 66,000–86,569 by headings and the tail: Listings 2–4 (the hand-written CoT demonstrations for 2Wiki, MuSiQue and IIRC) and the ACL Responsible-NLP checklist. Those pages hold no results. Page numbers below are PDF pages (p1 = proceedings p.10014).

CLAIMS
- claim: Retrieving step by step with the CoT beats one-step retrieval that uses only the question. The gains are larger with GPT3 than with Flan-T5-XXL.
  number: Flan-T5-XXL +7.9 / +14.3 / +3.5 / +10.2; GPT3 +11.3 / +22.6 / +12.5 / +21.2 recall points (HotpotQA / 2Wiki / MuSiQue / IIRC)
  setup: BM25 (Elasticsearch) is the base retriever. Open-domain test set of 500 sampled dev questions per dataset. Recall of gold paragraphs is measured with at most 15 paragraphs ("fixed-budget optimal recall"). K and M are tuned on 100 dev questions. Each figure is the mean of 3 demonstration sets.
  quote: "For Flan-T5-XXL, IRCoT improves our recall metric relative to one-step retrieval, on HotpotQA by 7.9, on 2WikiMultihopQA by 14.3, on MuSiQue by 3.5, and on IIRC by 10.2 points. For GPT3, this improvement is by 11.3, 22.6, 12.5, and 21.2 points, respectively."
  where: p6
- claim: Downstream QA F1 improves over one-step retrieval QA in every case but one: GPT3 on IIRC shows no gain.
  number: Flan-T5-XXL +9.4 / +15.3 / +5.0 / +2.5 F1; GPT3 +7.1 / +13.2 / +7.1 F1 (no gain on IIRC)
  setup: Same setup as above. The reader is the same LM: Direct prompting for Flan-T5 and CoT prompting for GPT3. Abstract headline: "up to 21 points" retrieval and "up to 15 points" QA.
  quote: "For Flan-T5-XXL, IRCoT QA outperforms OneR QA on HotpotQA by 9.4, on 2WikiMultihopQA by 15.3, on MuSiQue by 5.0 and IIRC by 2.5 F1 points. For GPT3, the corresponding numbers (except for IIRC) are 7.1, 13.2, and 7.1 F1 points."
  where: p6
- claim: Better retrieval does not always give better QA. On IIRC, GPT3 retrieval improved by 21 points but QA did not improve, likely because GPT3 already holds that knowledge in its parameters.
  number: 21 points
  quote: "For GPT3, IRCoT doesn't improve the QA score on IIRC, despite significantly improved retrieval (21 points as shown in Fig. 3). This is likely because IIRC relevant knowledge may already be present in GPT3, as also evidenced by its NoR QA score being similar."
  where: p6
- claim: A small model with interleaved retrieval beats a 58x larger model with one-step retrieval.
  number: 3B vs 175B (58X)
  setup: Flan-T5-XL (3B) with IRCoT vs GPT3 code-davinci-002 with OneR and NoR, on HotpotQA, 2Wiki and MuSiQue (IIRC skipped).
  quote: "IRCoT with a 3B model even outperforms OneR and NoR with a 58X larger 175B GPT3 model in all datasets."
  where: p8
- claim: Retrieval improves at every model size, but QA improves at every size except the smallest.
  number: 0.2B
  quote: "IRCoT with even the smallest model (0.2B) is better than OneR" ... "For all sizes except the smallest (0.2B), we see IRCoT QA is better than OneR QA."
  where: p7–8 (the Fig. 8/9 captions say "0.3B", which is inconsistent with the text)
- claim: Interleaving cuts factual errors in the generated reasoning chains.
  number: 50% (HotpotQA), 40% (2Wiki); sample of 40 questions per dataset
  setup: GPT3 CoTs, annotated by hand by the authors. A CoT counts as an error if at least one fact before "answer is:" is false.
  quote: "IRCoT reduces the factual errors over OneR by 50% on HotpotQA and 40% on 2WikiMultihopQA."
  where: p7
- claim: The gains hold out of distribution, with demonstrations from one dataset and evaluation on another.
  number: none (shown only in Figs. 5–6; no figures are given in the text)
  setup: Pairs of HotpotQA, 2Wiki and MuSiQue; IIRC excluded; retrieval uses the evaluation dataset's corpus.
  quote: "For all pairs of the datasets and for both Flan-T5-XXL and GPT3, we find the same trend as in the IID setting: IRCoT retrieval outperforms OneR (Fig. 5), and IRCoT QA outperforms both OneR QA and NoR QA (Fig. 6)."
  where: p6
- claim: Absolute F1 for the best readers (Table 4).
  number: GPT3 CoT reader: OneR 53.6 / 54.8 / 29.4 / 49.8 vs IRCoT 60.7 / 68.0 / 36.5 / 49.9. Flan-T5-XXL Direct reader: OneR 49.7 / 51.2 / 25.8 / 40.0 vs IRCoT 59.1 / 66.5 / 30.8 / 42.5
  quote: "IRCoT QA Direct 59.1± 0.9 66.5± 1.4 30.8± 0.2 42.5± 2.1 60.6± 1.0 63.5± 2.7 36.0± 0.5 47.9± 2.3CoT 52.0 ± 0.6 55.1± 1.0 24.9± 1.0 36.5± 1.3 60.7± 1.1 68.0± 1.5 36.5± 1.2 49.9± 1.1"
  where: p14, Table 4
- claim: In a leaderboard comparison the authors say is not head-to-head, IRCoT stayed state of the art on MuSiQue, but newer systems beat it elsewhere: DSP on HotpotQA by 2.0 and DecomP on 2Wiki by 2.8.
  number: 2.0, 2.8
  quote: "While IRCoT remains SOTA on MuSiQue, DSP outperforms it on HotpotQA by 2.0 points and the newer version of Decomp outperforms IRCoT on 2WikiMultihopQA by 2.8 points."
  where: p14, App. C / Table 3 (as of May 25, 2023)
- claim: A separate reader pass usually beats taking the answer from the retrieval-time CoT. It helps clearly for Flan-T5 but is mixed for GPT3.
  number: Flan-T5 59.1 vs 52.6 (HotpotQA); GPT3 68.0 vs 70.4 without the reader (2Wiki)
  quote: "For Flan-T5-XXL having a separate reader is significantly better. For GPT3, this is not always true"
  where: p15, App. F / Table 6
- claim: Mechanism and loop parameters. The loop retrieves K paragraphs with the question. It then alternates: generate one CoT sentence, then retrieve K more paragraphs using that sentence as the query. It stops on "answer is:" or after 8 steps, with at most 15 paragraphs in total.
  number: 8 steps; 15 paragraphs; K ∈ {2,4,6,8}
  quote: "If the generated CoT sentence has the "answer is:" string or the maximum number of steps 4 has been reached" / "4set to 8 in our experiments. 5set to 15 in our experiments."
  where: p4–5
- claim: Cost. Each CoT sentence costs one LLM call, plus one final reader call. The paper does not measure call counts or latency.
  number: none measured
  quote: "The performance gain of IRCoT retriever and QA (over OneR and ZeroR baselines) come with an additional computational cost. This is because IRCoT makes a separate call to an (L)LM for each sentence of CoT."
  where: p9, Limitations

LIMITS
- No measured cost. There are no LLM-call counts, token counts or latency anywhere. The cost is only conceded qualitatively. From the method, the cost is bounded by 8 reason steps plus 1 reader call; that is my inference, not a reported figure.
- The metric is non-standard. Retrieved sets are unranked, so MAP, DCG and Recall@k do not apply; recall is "fixed-budget optimal" with K tuned per system on dev (footnote 7, p5).
- Corpora for 2Wiki, MuSiQue and IIRC are built from the datasets' own paragraphs (139K–1.9M paragraphs), so they are not full open web. Only "answerable subsets" of MuSiQue and IIRC are used. Each test set is 500 questions.
- The retriever is BM25 only; dense retrievers and rerankers are not tested.
- The factual-error study is small: 40 questions per dataset, hand-annotated, with no agreement statistics.
- The OOD test covers 3 datasets only. Smaller models are not evaluated on IIRC.
- The authors concede the method needs CoT ability, which they say is less common under 20B. It also needs long context (8K for GPT3) and adds compute per sentence. They suggest future work on "dynamically deciding when to retrieve".
- Dated: code-davinci-002 "was deprecated by OpenAI after our submission making the reproduction of these experiments challenging". Comparisons with SelfAsk, ReAct and DecomP are not head-to-head (different corpora, LLMs and test subsets).

BUILDS ON
- Chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022); few-shot / Direct prompting (Brown et al., 2020); retrieve-and-read paradigm (Zhu et al., 2021); BM25 (Robertson et al., 2009).
- Supervised iterative multi-hop retrieval: Das et al. (2019), Feldman and El-Yaniv (2019), Xiong et al. (2021) (multi-hop DPR, from Karpukhin et al., 2020), Khattab et al. (2021) Baleen, Asai et al. (2020), GoldEn (Qi et al., 2019), WebGPT (Nakano et al., 2021).
- Prompting contemporaries: SelfAsk (Press et al., 2022), DecomP (Khot et al., 2023), ReAct (Yao et al., 2022), RECITE (Sun et al., 2022), Internet-Augmented QA (Lazaridou et al., 2022), DSP (Khattab et al., 2023).
- Single-retrieval RAG it contrasts with: Lewis et al., 2020; Guu et al., 2020; Borgeaud et al., 2022; Izacard et al., 2022.

CODE (reason-step prompt template, p4)
```
Wikipedia Title: <Page Title>
<Paragraph Text>
...
Q: <Question>
A: <CoT-Sent-1> ... <CoT-Sent-n>
```
"for each reason-step, we only take the first generated sentence and discard the rest." (p5)

FIGURES
- Fig. 2, p4, is the best candidate. "IRCoT interleaves chain-of-thought (CoT) generation and retrieval steps ... (i) reason-step generates next CoT sentence ... (ii) retrieve-step retrieves K more paragraphs based on the last CoT sentence. The process terminates when the generated CoT has "answer is" or the number of steps exceeds a threshold." It shows the Retrieve(Q) → T1 → Retrieve(T1) → T2 loop on one worked example, which makes the contrast between single-pass and iterative retrieval clear at a glance.
- Fig. 1, p1, is the simpler alternative: the "Lost Gravity → Mack Rides → Germany" example, showing why the second hop cannot be retrieved from the question alone.
- Figs. 3 and 9 (p6, p8) are bar and scaling plots of the numbers above. Fig. 9 supports the "3B beats 58x larger" point.

PROBLEMS
- The extraction is clean apart from minor mojibake in Listing 1 ("Leeâ˘A¸ SEnfield"). Table 4's rows are run together in the extraction ("2.3CoT 52.0"), but the values parse.
- The paper is internally inconsistent on the smallest model: the text says 0.2B, the Fig. 8/9 captions say 0.3B.
- The OOD gains appear only in bar charts (Figs. 5–6). The text gives no numbers, so none are quoted.
- No embedded instructions were found.
